title: Latest FIFA men’s world rankings: France go top, USMNT fall to 16th
content:
France have taken top spot in the latest edition of FIFA’s men’s soccer world rankings following the March international break.

It is the first time since September 2018 that France have been ranked No 1 by the world governing body.

Having already qualified for the 2026 World Cup, Didier Deschamps’ team beat Brazil 2-1 and Colombia 3-1 in friendly matches last month and have risen two places from third.

They replace Spain in top spot, with the European champions dropping to second after a six-month spell leading the rankings. World champions Argentina, despite friendly wins over Mauritania and Zambia, have fallen to third.

The USMNT has dropped one place to 16th, swapping positions with its World Cup co-host Mexico, following a 5-2 loss against Belgium and a 2-0 defeat to Portugal. Mauricio Pochettino’s side has won just four of its last nine games. The U.S. has been ranked outside of the top 10 since August 2021.

Thomas Tuchel’s England remain in fourth place, despite a 1-1 draw against Uruguay and a 1-0 loss to Japan. Portugal have moved up to fifth, swapping places with Brazil in the only other movement in the top 10.

Senegal, who defeated Peru and The Gambia in friendlies, have dropped two positions to 14th. FIFA’s rankings show that they were neither awarded nor deducted any points for the Africa Cup of Nations final against Morocco, which they won 1-0 in January but were ruled to have forfeited last month.

The biggest risers inside the top 50 were Sweden, who jumped four places to No 38, while Scotland — who suffered defeats against Japan and Ivory Coast — have fallen five positions to No 43.

FIFA’s ranking system is based on its ‘SUM’ algorithm which either adds or removes points based on results, the importance of a match (a World Cup win earns more points than a friendly, for example) and the difference in ranking positions between teams entering a match.
